result:
If I could alter one fundamental aspect of the world, it would be to dissolve the illusion of separation between human minds—to give every person the involuntary, visceral capacity to feel the internal reality of another. 

Most human suffering, cruelty, and apathy do not stem from inherent malice, but from abstraction. Other people are treated as concepts, statistics, obstacles, or enemies simply because it is impossible to sit inside their consciousness and feel their grief, their terror, or their joy. Dehumanization is only possible because of the thick walls built around the individual self.

If causing harm instantly meant experiencing the exact weight of that harm yourself, and if witnessing suffering carried the undeniable sting of that reality, cruelty would become functionally obsolete. Empathy would no longer be a moral aspiration or a fragile virtue; it would be an inescapable law of human interaction.
